## `client.tables`

The `tables` resource of the platform API.

### `client.tables.list`

Signature: `client.tables.list(environment: str, namespace: str, *, model_kind: str | None = None, lang: str | None = None) -> list[Table]`

List the tables in a namespace.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | Dot-joined namespace path. |
| `model_kind` | `str | None` | `None` | Only the tables whose asset header declares this kind: ``fact``, ``dimension``, ``wide`` or ``staging``. Every table when `None`. |
| `lang` | `str | None` | `None` | The language of the texts, such as ``de`` or ``fr-CH``; without it, your profile's language, else the instance's main language. |

Returns: `list of Table`. Every table in the namespace that you may read.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the namespace does not exist. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If `model_kind` is not one of the kinds, or `lang` is not a language tag. |

### `client.tables.health`

Signature: `client.tables.health(environment: str, qualified_name: str, *, days: int | None = None, readers: bool = True) -> TableHealth`

Show a table's last maintenance, the newest result of each check, and its readers.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined `"namespace.table"` name. |
| `days` | `int | None` | `None` | The window of the readers in days, from 1 to the server's kept period (90 by default); the server's default window (30) when `None`. |
| `readers` | `bool` | `True` | `False` asks the server to leave the readers out: no names and no audit entry on the server. `True` by default. A server older than this release ignores the parameter: it still returns the readers and still writes the view audit. |

Returns: `TableHealth`. The health. `readers` is `None` when `readers` is `False`, or unless you may see the table's grants (the `ADMIN` role).

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If no such table exists. |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | Without `READ_TABLE` on the table. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If `days` is outside the range; the message names it. |

### `client.tables.describe`

Signature: `client.tables.describe(environment: str, qualified_name: str, description: str | None = UNSET, *, label: str | None = UNSET, column: str | None = None, lang: str | None = None, label_language: str | None = None) -> Table`

Set the description or label of a table or one of its columns, or reset them.

A text set here is shown instead of the one a deploy publishes from the asset header or a translation file, and a deploy never replaces it. Resetting (`None`) removes it, so the project's text shows again; a field you leave out stays as it is. Without `lang`, the edit is in the table's main language; `label_language` puts the label in another language than the description. Needs to own the table or hold `DROP_TABLE` on it.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined `"namespace.table"` name. |
| `description` | `str | None` | `UNSET` | The new text (1 to 4,000 characters, not blank), or `None` to reset. |
| `label` | `str | None` | `UNSET` | The new label (one line, 1 to 100 characters), or `None` to reset. |
| `column` | `str | None` | `None` | A column of the table to describe instead of the table. |
| `lang` | `str | None` | `None` | The language edited, such as `"fr"`; also the language of the returned texts. Without it, the edit is in the table's main language and the returned texts follow your profile's language, then the server's main language. |
| `label_language` | `str | None` | `None` | The language the label is edited in, such as `"en"`, when it is not `lang`'s; without it, the label is edited in the same language as the description. Needs `label`. |

Returns: `Table`. The table, with the texts it shows now.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `ValueError` | If neither `description` nor `label` is given, or `label_language` without `label`. |
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the table, or the column, does not exist. |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | Without the right to describe the table. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If a text breaks its rules, or `lang` or `label_language` is not a language tag. |
| `lakana.InvalidResponse` | With `label_language`, when the server is older than it and edited the label in the description's language instead; the message names that language. A label in another language is read back once to check this. |

### `client.tables.delete`

Signature: `client.tables.delete(environment: str, qualified_name: str, *, purge: bool = False, break_glass_reason: str | None = None) -> None`

Drop a table. A managed table's files are kept for the undo period, then deleted.

Within the server's undo period (`LAKANA_TABLES__UNDO_DAYS`, 7 days by default) `undrop` restores the table with its data, grants, row filters and column masks. An external table's files and a view are never deleted.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined `"namespace.table"` name. |
| `purge` | `bool` | `False` | Delete the files at the server's next sweep instead; the table cannot be restored. |
| `break_glass_reason` | `str | None` | `None` | Write to a protected environment outside a run: 10-500 characters, needs `MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT`, audited. The next run of the deployed code may overwrite the fix. |

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If no such table exists. |
| `lakana.Conflict` | If a deployed project builds the table or view: remove its asset in git and deploy, then drop it. The message names the file to someone who may read it. |

### `client.tables.undrop`

Signature: `client.tables.undrop(environment: str, qualified_name: str, *, new_name: str | None = None, break_glass_reason: str | None = None) -> Table`

Restore a dropped table within its undo period: the same table, data and policies.

Needs `DROP_TABLE` and `CREATE_TABLE` on the namespace. When the name was dropped more than once, the newest drop comes back; restore an older one under another name.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined `"namespace.table"` name the table had. |
| `new_name` | `str | None` | `None` | Restore it under this name in the same namespace, when its own name is taken. |
| `break_glass_reason` | `str | None` | `None` | Write to a protected environment outside a run: 10-500 characters, needs `MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT`, audited. |

Returns: `Table`. The restored table.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If no dropped table of that name can be restored, or its namespace is gone. |
| `lakana.Conflict` | If a table of the name exists (pass `new_name`), the undo period has ended, or the files are being deleted. |

### `client.tables.rebuild`

Signature: `client.tables.rebuild(environment: str, qualified_name: str, *, reason: str, break_glass_reason: str | None = None) -> TableRebuild`

Rebuild a table a deployed project builds: drop it and queue a run of its asset.

The drop keeps the undo period, so `undrop` restores the old table within it. Needs `DROP_TABLE` on the table and `RUN` on the environment.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined `"namespace.table"` name. |
| `reason` | `str` | required | Why: 10-500 characters on one line, recorded in the audit log. |
| `break_glass_reason` | `str | None` | `None` | Rebuild in a protected environment: 10-500 characters, needs `MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT`, audited. The run writes as the deployment's run principal. |

Returns: `TableRebuild`. The table, the queued run and the file that builds it.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If no such table exists. |
| `lakana.Conflict` | If it is an artifact, no deployed project builds it (drop it instead), another run of the project is active (nothing was dropped; rebuild again once it ends), or a protected environment has no run principal. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If the reason is not 10-500 characters on one line. |

### `client.tables.set_retention`

Signature: `client.tables.set_retention(environment: str, qualified_name: str, *, days: int | None = None, on: date | None = None, never: bool = False) -> TableRetention`

Set when a managed table expires. Give exactly one of `days`, `on` and `never`.

An expired table is dropped by the server's sweep and can be restored with `undrop` during the undo period. The table's owner may always set it. Anyone else needs `DROP_TABLE` to make the table expire earlier (or at all), and `WRITE_TABLE` to make it expire later or never.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined `"namespace.table"` name. |
| `days` | `int | None` | `None` | Expire this many days (1 to 3,650) after the table's last activity: the later of its last change and its last recorded read. |
| `on` | `date | None` | `None` | Expire from midnight UTC of this day on; it must be after today. |
| `never` | `bool` | `False` | Never expire, whatever the environment's retention says. |

Returns: `TableRetention`. The retention now.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If no such table exists. |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | Without the right the change needs. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | Unless exactly one valid rule is given; for anything but a managed table; and in a protected environment, whose tables never expire. |

### `client.tables.create`

Signature: `client.tables.create(environment: str, qualified_name: str, schema: pa.Schema | list[dict[str, Any]], *, break_glass_reason: str | None = None) -> Table`

Create a managed (Iceberg) table from a schema.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined `"namespace.table"` name. |
| `schema` | `pa.Schema | list[dict[str, Any]]` | required | The table's columns: a `pyarrow.Schema`, anything exposing the Arrow C schema interface such as a polars `Schema` (the SDK turns both into the list of columns the server takes), or an already-JSON-shaped list of `{"name", "type", "nullable"}` dicts. A polars `Schema` needs Polars 1.37 or newer; with an older Polars pass `pyarrow.schema(...)` or a list of columns instead. |
| `break_glass_reason` | `str | None` | `None` | Write to a protected environment outside a run: 10-500 characters, needs `MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT`, audited. The next run of the deployed code may overwrite the fix. |

Returns: `Table`. The created table.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the namespace does not exist. |
| `lakana.Conflict` | If a table of this name already exists. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If `schema` names a column type the SDK or server cannot represent, or is a polars `Schema` and the installed Polars is older than 1.37 (it cannot export its schema to Arrow). |
| `TypeError` | If `schema` is neither a list nor anything `pyarrow.schema` accepts (and is not a polars `Schema`). |

### `client.tables.append`

Signature: `client.tables.append(environment: str, qualified_name: str, data: pa.Table | pa.RecordBatch | object, *, sources: Sequence[str] | None = None, source_versions: Mapping[str, int] | None = None, break_glass_reason: str | None = None, expected_snapshot_id: int | str | None = None) -> AppendResult`

Append rows to a managed table.

Serialises `data` as an uncompressed Arrow IPC stream and retries the request exactly once if the server reports a `Conflict` (409) — another writer committed to the table first, and a retry against the table's now-current state is a reasonable default for a client that just wants its rows written.

Sent with its own timeout of 300 seconds, longer than `Client`'s general default, since an append body can be large enough that the general default is not a reasonable bound. **A timeout here is ambiguous, not a clean failure**: the server may have already committed the append by the time the client gives up waiting for a response, so a caller that blindly retries a timed-out append can duplicate rows — unlike the `Conflict` retry below, which is safe precisely because a conflict response proves nothing was committed by *this* request.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined `"namespace.table"` name. |
| `data` | `pa.Table | pa.RecordBatch | object` | required | The rows to append: a `pa.Table`, a `pa.RecordBatch`, or anything `pyarrow.table()` accepts. |
| `sources` | `Sequence[str] | None` | `None` | Dotted names of the tables `data` was derived from, recorded as lineage. Each must exist and be readable by the caller. |
| `source_versions` | `Mapping[str, int] | None` | `None` | The version of each source that is an artifact, by dotted name, when the caller read a specific one; the lineage records it instead of the current version. |
| `break_glass_reason` | `str | None` | `None` | Write to a protected environment outside a run: 10-500 characters, needs `MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT`, audited. The next run of the deployed code may overwrite the fix. |
| `expected_snapshot_id` | `int | str | None` | `None` | The table's current snapshot as you read it (`Table.snapshot_id`), or ``"none"`` for "no snapshot yet". The write commits only while that still holds; otherwise `Conflict` is raised and nothing is retried. |

Returns: `AppendResult`. How many rows and files were written, and the committed snapshot's id.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the table does not exist. |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | If the caller may not write to this table. |
| `lakana.Conflict` | If a second attempt, after one retry, still conflicts; or at once when `expected_snapshot_id` no longer matches. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If the data's schema does not match the table's; an unsupported Arrow type is used; or a nanosecond-precision timestamp column would be truncated by the platform API's microsecond precision. |

### `client.tables.replace`

Signature: `client.tables.replace(environment: str, qualified_name: str, data: pa.Table | pa.RecordBatch | object, *, evolve_schema: bool = False, sources: Sequence[str] | None = None, source_versions: Mapping[str, int] | None = None, break_glass_reason: str | None = None, expected_snapshot_id: int | str | None = None) -> WriteResult`

Replace every row of a managed table.

One snapshot: readers see the old rows or the new ones, never a mix, and time travel keeps the old data. Serialised and retried exactly like `append`; a timeout is just as ambiguous here.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined `"namespace.table"` name. |
| `data` | `pa.Table | pa.RecordBatch | object` | required | The new rows: a `pa.Table`, a `pa.RecordBatch`, or anything `pyarrow.table()` accepts. |
| `evolve_schema` | `bool` | `False` | Let the table adopt `data`'s schema instead of refusing a mismatch. |
| `sources` | `Sequence[str] | None` | `None` | Dotted names of the tables `data` was derived from. |
| `source_versions` | `Mapping[str, int] | None` | `None` | The version of each source that is an artifact, by dotted name, when the caller read a specific one. |
| `break_glass_reason` | `str | None` | `None` | Write to a protected environment outside a run: 10-500 characters, needs `MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT`, audited. The next run of the deployed code may overwrite the fix. |
| `expected_snapshot_id` | `int | str | None` | `None` | The table's current snapshot as you read it (`Table.snapshot_id`), or ``"none"`` for "no snapshot yet". The write commits only while that still holds; otherwise `Conflict` is raised and nothing is retried. On `replace`, ``"none"`` also creates a missing table from `data`. |

Returns: `WriteResult`. What was written, and how the schema changed.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the table or a source does not exist. |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | If the caller may not write the table or read a source. |
| `lakana.Conflict` | If a second attempt, after one retry, still conflicts; or at once when `expected_snapshot_id` no longer matches. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If `data` doesn't match the table and `evolve_schema` is off. |

### `client.tables.upload_limit`

Signature: `client.tables.upload_limit() -> int | None`

Ask the server for the largest Arrow body one write may send.

Returns: `int or None`. `LAKANA_APPEND__MAX_BYTES` of the server, or `None` when it does not say (an older server); its own 413 then applies.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.LakanaConnectionError` | If the server could not be reached. |

### `client.tables.load`

Signature: `client.tables.load(environment: str, qualified_name: str, data: pa.Table | pa.RecordBatch | object, *, write: str = 'replace', expected_snapshot_id: int | str | None = None, break_glass_reason: str | None = None, dry_run: bool = False) -> LoadResult`

Load rows into a table of the bronze layer, as `lakana load` does.

The server refuses a table whose first namespace segment is not `bronze`, before it reads the rows, with a `ValidationError` that says to load into `bronze.<name>` and transform it with an asset. Loads are for one-off files; anything that runs again belongs in an asset. Never retried on a conflict: a load always names the snapshot it expects.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined `"bronze.table"` (or a deeper `"bronze.…"`) name. |
| `data` | `pa.Table | pa.RecordBatch | object` | required | The rows: a `pa.Table`, a `pa.RecordBatch`, or anything `pyarrow.table()` accepts. For a dry run, an empty table of the schema to check. |
| `write` | `str` | `'replace'` | ``replace`` (the default) or ``append``. A first load (``expected_snapshot_id= "none"``) creates the table whichever is given. |
| `expected_snapshot_id` | `int | str | None` | `None` | The table's current snapshot as you read it (`Table.snapshot_id`), or ``"none"`` for a table that does not exist yet, which the load then creates. Without it, a missing table is a `NotFound` that says to pass ``"none"``. |
| `break_glass_reason` | `str | None` | `None` | Write to a protected environment outside a run: 10-500 characters, needs `MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT`, audited. |
| `dry_run` | `bool` | `False` | Run every check, the schema against an existing table included, and write nothing. |

Returns: `LoadResult`. What was written, and whether the table was created.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.ValidationError` | For a target outside bronze, or rows the table refuses. |
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the namespace does not exist (the message names the command that creates it), or the table does not and `expected_snapshot_id` is not ``"none"`` (the message says to pass it). |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | Without `WRITE_TABLE`, without `CREATE_TABLE` for a first load, or in a protected environment without `break_glass_reason` and `MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT`; a dry run is refused the same way. |
| `lakana.Conflict` | If the table's snapshot is no longer `expected_snapshot_id`. |

### `client.tables.merge`

Signature: `client.tables.merge(environment: str, qualified_name: str, data: pa.Table | pa.RecordBatch | object, *, key: str | Sequence[str], sources: Sequence[str] | None = None, source_versions: Mapping[str, int] | None = None, break_glass_reason: str | None = None, expected_snapshot_id: int | str | None = None) -> MergeResult`

Merge rows into a managed table on a key.

A row whose `key` matches a row of the table replaces it; any other row is inserted; nothing is deleted. One snapshot: readers see the table before or after, never a half. The rows must not repeat a key and no key may be null; a key that matches two rows of the table is refused too. Needs `WRITE_TABLE` and `READ_TABLE`, and is refused while a row filter or column mask on the table applies to you. A key of several columns takes at most 5,000 rows per call. Serialised, sent and retried exactly like `append`, and a timeout is just as ambiguous here (a merge sent twice is harmless: the second changes nothing).

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined `"namespace.table"` name. |
| `data` | `pa.Table | pa.RecordBatch | object` | required | The rows: a `pa.Table`, a `pa.RecordBatch`, or anything `pyarrow.table()` accepts. |
| `key` | `str | Sequence[str]` | required | The column, or the columns, that identify a row. |
| `sources` | `Sequence[str] | None` | `None` | Dotted names of the tables `data` was derived from, recorded as lineage. Each must exist and be readable by the caller. |
| `source_versions` | `Mapping[str, int] | None` | `None` | The version of each source that is an artifact, by dotted name, when the caller read a specific one. |
| `break_glass_reason` | `str | None` | `None` | Write to a protected environment outside a run: 10-500 characters, needs `MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT`, audited. The next run of the deployed code may overwrite the fix. |
| `expected_snapshot_id` | `int | str | None` | `None` | The table's current snapshot as you read it (`Table.snapshot_id`), or ``"none"`` for "no snapshot yet". The merge commits only while that still holds; otherwise `Conflict` is raised and nothing is retried. ``"none"`` also creates a missing table from `data`. |

Returns: `MergeResult`. The committed snapshot's id and how many rows were inserted and updated.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `ValueError` | If `key` names no column; nothing is sent. |
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the table or a source does not exist. |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | If the caller may not write the table or read a source. |
| `lakana.Conflict` | If a second attempt, after one retry, still conflicts; or at once when `expected_snapshot_id` no longer matches. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If a key column is missing, a key is null or repeats (the message gives the count of rows, never a value), a key of several columns comes with more than 5,000 rows, `data` does not match the table, or a row filter or column mask applies to you. |

### `client.tables.history`

Signature: `client.tables.history(environment: str, qualified_name: str, data: pa.Table | pa.RecordBatch | object, *, key: str | Sequence[str], valid_from: str | None = None, close_missing: bool = False, sources: Sequence[str] | None = None, source_versions: Mapping[str, int] | None = None, break_glass_reason: str | None = None, expected_snapshot_id: int | str | None = None) -> HistoryResult`

Keep the versions of a dimension's rows: send the current state of every row.

Against the table's open versions, a new key opens a version, a key whose values changed closes its version and opens a new one, and an unchanged key is left alone; with `close_missing`, a key the rows lack is closed. Nothing is deleted. One snapshot. A Python asset with ``write="history"`` calls this for you. A key's first version always starts at 0001-01-01 UTC, so that every row of a fact finds it; a later version sent by hand starts at the time of the call unless `valid_from` names a column. Needs `WRITE_TABLE` and `READ_TABLE`, and is refused while a row filter or column mask on the table applies to you. Serialised, sent and retried exactly like `merge` (a write sent twice changes nothing the second time).

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined `"namespace.table"` name. |
| `data` | `pa.Table | pa.RecordBatch | object` | required | The rows: a `pa.Table`, a `pa.RecordBatch`, or anything `pyarrow.table()` accepts. |
| `key` | `str | Sequence[str]` | required | The column, or the columns, that identify a row (the natural key). |
| `valid_from` | `str | None` | `None` | The column each later version's start is read from (a date or a timestamp), or `None` for the time the call's run began; a key's first version starts at 0001-01-01 UTC either way. |
| `close_missing` | `bool` | `False` | Close the open version of each key the rows lack. |
| `sources` | `Sequence[str] | None` | `None` | Dotted names of the tables `data` was derived from, recorded as lineage. |
| `source_versions` | `Mapping[str, int] | None` | `None` | The version of each source that is an artifact, by dotted name. |
| `break_glass_reason` | `str | None` | `None` | Write to a protected environment outside a run: 10-500 characters, audited. |
| `expected_snapshot_id` | `int | str | None` | `None` | The table's current snapshot as you read it, or ``"none"``, which also creates a missing table with every row as an open version. |

Returns: `HistoryResult`. The committed snapshot's id and the counts.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `ValueError` | If `key` names no column; nothing is sent. |
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the table or a source does not exist. |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | If the caller may not write or read the table or read a source. |
| `lakana.Conflict` | If a second attempt, after one retry, still conflicts; or at once when `expected_snapshot_id` no longer matches. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | For what a history write refuses (the message gives counts, never values). |

### `client.tables.lineage`

Signature: `client.tables.lineage(environment: str, qualified_name: str, *, direction: str = 'upstream', depth: int = 3) -> Lineage`

Walk a table's persisted lineage.

Nodes the caller can't read are left out and counted in `hidden_nodes`; the walk never passes through one.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined `"namespace.table"` name. |
| `direction` | `str` | `'upstream'` | `"upstream"` (what fed it) or `"downstream"` (what it fed). |
| `depth` | `int` | `3` | Hops to walk, 1 to 10. |

Returns: `Lineage`. The graph.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the table does not exist. |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | If the caller can't read the table. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If `direction` or `depth` is out of range. |

### `client.tables.references`

Signature: `client.tables.references(environment: str, qualified_name: str) -> TableReferences`

Show what a table's header says it references, and which tables reference it.

These are the references the model declares (`references:`), not lineage. A reference whose target, or whose referencing table, you may not read is counted, never named.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined `"namespace.table"` name. |

Returns: `TableReferences`. Outgoing and incoming references.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the table does not exist. |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | If you may not read the table. |

### `client.tables.maintain`

Signature: `client.tables.maintain(environment: str, qualified_name: str, *, keep_days: int = 7, keep_last: int = 5, dry_run: bool = False, older_than_hours: int = 72) -> QueryRun`

Queue maintenance for a table: expire old snapshots, delete orphans.

A worker runs it; poll the returned handle, whose finished status carries `maintenance["report"]`. The report's `conflict` is `True` when the table changed during maintenance and nothing was applied (retry); its `note` says in words why part of the run was skipped; its `tags_removed` lists the tags of failed checks (older than seven days) that were removed.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined `"namespace.table"` name. |
| `keep_days` | `int` | `7` | Snapshots younger than this many days are kept. |
| `keep_last` | `int` | `5` | The most recent this many snapshots are kept. |
| `dry_run` | `bool` | `False` | Report what would happen without changing anything. |
| `older_than_hours` | `int` | `72` | Unreferenced files younger than this many hours are never deleted (default 72, at least 1, at most 87600). |

Returns: `QueryRun`. A handle to the maintenance run.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the table does not exist. |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | Without MAINTAIN_TABLE on the table or SUBMIT_QUERY on the environment. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If `keep_days` is negative, `keep_last` is below 1, or `older_than_hours` is outside 1 to 87600. |

### `client.tables.preview`

Signature: `client.tables.preview(environment: str, qualified_name: str) -> QueryRun`

Queue a preview of a table's first 100 rows, read as you.

A worker runs it as a query of yours, so your row filters and column masks apply. Poll the returned handle, then read the rows with `QueryRun.page()`, whose `masked_columns` names the columns that were masked for you.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined `"namespace.table"` name. |

Returns: `QueryRun`. A handle to the preview run.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the table does not exist. |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | Without the right to run queries in the environment, or to read the table. |
| `lakana.Conflict` | If the name is an artifact's, which holds files, not rows, or its namespace or table name contains a dot, which a query cannot name yet; the message names the next step. |

### `client.tables.definition`

Signature: `client.tables.definition(environment: str, qualified_name: str) -> TableDefinition`

Say where the environment's current deployment defines a table.

The answer is the deployed commit's file and line, never the branch head's, and a link to the line on the repository's git host when one can be built.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined `"namespace.table"` name. |

Returns: `TableDefinition`. The location; `defined` is `False` for a table created or renamed outside a project.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the environment does not exist, or a table you may read is gone (dropped). |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | If the table does not exist or you may not read it: the two answers are the same. |

### `client.tables.definition_file`

Signature: `client.tables.definition_file(environment: str, qualified_name: str) -> TableDefinitionFile`

Read the file that defines a table, as the current deployment recorded it.

The text is returned only to someone who may read the environment and every table the file uses, without a row filter or column mask; anyone else gets the location and a `reason`. Reading the text is recorded in the audit log.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined `"namespace.table"` name. |

Returns: `TableDefinitionFile`. The location with the text, or with the `reason` and `message` it is not shown.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the environment does not exist, or a table you may read is gone (dropped). |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | If the table does not exist or you may not read it: the two answers are the same. |
| `lakana.ServerError` | With status 503 when the read could not be recorded in the audit log; try again. |
